statement: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero. The test is v^T w = 0.

anchors.quote: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero

statement: For orthogonal vectors v and w (v^T w = 0), the squared lengths add: ||v||^2 + ||w||^2 = ||v + w||^2. This is the right-triangle relation a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

anchors.quote: for a right triangle with sides v and w
\| \boldsymbol {v} \| ^ {2} + \| \boldsymbol {w} \| ^ {2} = \| \boldsymbol {v} + \boldsymbol {w} \| ^ {2}.

statement: Two subspaces V and W are orthogonal if every vector v in V is perpendicular to every vector w in W, i.e. v^T w = 0 for all such pairs.

anchors.quote: Two subspaces V and $W$ of a vector space are orthogonal if every vector v in V is perpendicular to every vector w in $W$
Subspaces V and Ware orthogonal if every v in Vis orthogonal to every win W.

statement: The row space C(A^T) and the nullspace N(A) are orthogonal subspaces of R^n. Every row of A is perpendicular to every solution of Ax = 0.

name_zh: 列空间与左零空间正交
statement: The column space C(A) and the left nullspace N(A^T) are always orthogonal subspaces of R^m. Every vector in N(A^T) is perpendicular to every column of A.

name_en: Only the zero vector lies in two orthogonal subspaces
name_zh: 两个正交子空间只共有零向量
statement: When a vector is in two orthogonal subspaces it must be zero, since it is perpendicular to itself. A vector orthogonal to itself is the zero vector.

anchors.quote: When a vector is in two orthogonal subspaces, it must be zero. It is perpendicular to itself.
If a vector v is orthogonal to itself then v is the zero vector.

statement: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V contains every vector perpendicular to V. The nullspace complement N(A)^perp is exactly the row space C(A^T).

anchors.quote: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V contains every vector that is perpendicular to V
We conclude that the nullspace complement $N ( A ) ^ { \perp }$ is exactly the row space

name_en: Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, Part 2
name_zh: 线性代数基本定理第二部分
statement: N(A) is the orthogonal complement of the row space C(A^T) in R^n, and N(A^T) is the orthogonal complement of the column space C(A) in R^m. This is the perpendicularity of the four subspaces.
aliases: Part 2 of the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra

anchors.quote: This perpendicularity of subspaces is Part 2 of the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra.
$N ( A )$ is the orthogonal complement of the row space $C ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } )$

name_en: Splitting a vector into row-space and nullspace components
name_zh: 向量分解为行空间与零空间分量
statement: Because the row space and nullspace are orthogonal complements, every x in R^n splits uniquely as x = x_r + x_n, a row space component plus a nullspace component.

anchors.quote: every x can be split into a row space component
Each x is the sum $x _ { r } + x _ { n }$ of a row space vector

name_en: A is invertible from row space to column space
name_zh: A 在行空间到列空间上可逆
statement: Every vector b in the column space comes from one and only one vector x_r in the row space. From the row space to the column space, A acts as an invertible (r by r) map.

anchors.quote: Every vector b in the column space comes from one and only one vector
From the row space to the column space, $A$ is invertible.

statement: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V is denoted V^perp, pronounced "V perp".

anchors.quote: This orthogonal subspace is denoted by $V ^ { \perp }$ (pronounced "V perp").

name_en: Dot product written as v^T w
statement: The dot product of v and w is written v . w = v^T w, so the orthogonality condition is v^T w = 0.

anchors.quote: their dot product is zero: $\boldsymbol { v } \boldsymbol { \cdot w } = \boldsymbol { v } ^ { \mathrm { T } } \boldsymbol { w } = \boldsymbol { 0 }$
$v ^ { \mathrm { T } } w = 0$ for all v in V and all w in W.
